newsitem.title: ITALY: Public relations expected to boom in Italy -survey.
newsitem.headline: Public relations expected to boom in Italy -survey.

text.p: The public relations business is expected to grow rapidly in Italy, where companies are having to get a grip on communication skills like never before, a survey said on Thursday.
The report, published by Shandwick Italia and based on a survey of some 1,200 companies, showed the public relations sector also faced serious challenges in Italy.
Shandwick Italia is wholly owned by London-based Shandwick International Plc, the world's biggest independent public relations agency network.
The head of Shandwick Italia said the survey showed the public relations sector had to rethink its strategy and purpose because people believed less and less in the media and in advertising.

"Faced with a vast mass of messages, diminished media credibility and doubts about advertising effectiveness, we must rethink our professional approach, not only in light of the extraordinary technological changes which have occurred but also in terms of methods and techniques to use," Furio Garbagnati, Chairman of Shandwick Italia said, commenting on the survey.
According to 98 percent of those polled, the public relations sector will take off in Italy, but only if it becomes more personal, creative, international, ethically transparent and professional.
The PR sector should also broaden its range of services and prices, and increase the use of new technology, those surveyed said.
Although 79 percent of the companies surveyed said they hired public relations agencies in 1996, 88 percent said PR was often used in a banal and inappropriate way.
